Evidence: Union Health Minister Mansukh Mandaviya stated that India does not agree with the WHO's estimate of Covid-19 deaths, which is 4.7 million. He emphasized that India records its Covid-related deaths through a transparent and legal process, governed by the Births and Deaths Registration Act, 1969. A resolution was passed at the 14th Conference of the Central Council of Health & Family Welfare, affirming India's disagreement with the WHO's mortality estimate. Mandaviya highlighted the robustness of the data provided by states and union territories, asserting that it is correct and authentic (Source 1).
Justification: The retrieved evidence directly supports the claim that India does not agree with the WHO's estimate of Covid-19 deaths. Union Health Minister Mansukh Mandaviya explicitly stated this disagreement and referenced a resolution passed by the Central Council of Health & Family Welfare to that effect. The evidence confirms that India maintains its own process for recording deaths, which it considers reliable, thus substantiating the claim.
